title: Best Time to Visit Kalimpong, Month by Month
meta_description: When to visit Kalimpong, Lava and Lolegaon: Kanchenjunga views, monsoon landslides, the Neora Valley closure, snow at Lava, festivals and Puja crowds.
summary: The best time to visit Kalimpong is October to mid-December, when the monsoon has cleared and Kanchenjunga shows on most mornings. March to May is the second window, warmer and hazier. June to September brings heavy rain, landslides on NH10 and the Neora Valley closure. January and February are cold, clear and quiet.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Come between October and mid-December if you can. The rain has washed the dust out of the air, the mornings are cold and dry, and Kanchenjunga stands clear above the Teesta valley from Deolo, Durpin and the village ridges at Rishyap, Charkhole and Icchey Gaon. This is also the season of Dashain and Tihar, so book early for the October holidays.

March to May is our second choice. Days are warm, the nurseries are in flower and the forests around Lava fill with birds, but haze often hides the mountains by mid-morning. January and February are cold and quiet, with the clearest skies of all on good days and a chance of snow at Lava and Rishyap. June to September is the monsoon: green, wet and the hardest time to move around, with Neora Valley National Park closed.

If you have one purpose, let it choose the month for you. For mountain views, come in November. For flowers, birds and forest walks, come in April. For a chance of snow in the villages, come in January or February and keep your dates loose. For the lowest prices with roads still mostly open, come in late February or the first half of March. For festivals, plan around Losar, Dashain and Tihar, or the Lepcha gatherings of December.

sections.heading: October to mid-December: the clear season
paras: This is when Kalimpong looks the way people imagine it. After the last monsoon showers in late September or early October, the air clears and the snow peaks of the Kanchenjunga range sit on the northern skyline from first light until the clouds build around 10 or 11 am. Sunrise points such as Tiffin Dara above Rishyap, Jhandi Dara near Lolegaon and Ramitey Dara above Sillery Gaon earn their early starts in these weeks.

Days in town are pleasant for walking and nights need a jacket. November is usually the steadiest month: Puja holidaymakers have gone home, rates settle, and Neora Valley has reopened after the monsoon closure, with the forest still wet and green. By mid-December the cold sets in properly and the villages above 1,800 m become quiet.

sections.heading: Winter: cold mornings and snow at Lava
paras: January and February suit travellers who do not mind the cold. Kalimpong town very rarely sees snow, but Lava and Rishyap get a dusting or more in some winters. Snow is never guaranteed, and when it comes, the Algarah to Lava road can be slippery for a day or two.

Homestays in the higher villages light bonfires and hand out extra quilts, but rooms are not heated, so pack thermals, a warm hat and socks for sleeping. In return you get the clearest skies of the year on good days, low prices and roads without holiday traffic.

Days are short in mid-winter. The sun is up a little after 6 am and it is dark by about 5 pm, so plan village transfers for the morning and be at your homestay before dusk. Shared jeeps to Lava and Pedong thin out early in the afternoon, and drivers prefer not to run the forest roads after dark when frost is likely.

sections.heading: Spring and the pre-monsoon haze
paras: From March the hills warm up. The orchid and cactus nurseries that made Kalimpong a flower town are at their best in spring, and the forests around Lava, Kolakham and Neora Valley are busy with birds. This is a good season for walking: forest trails are dry, and the canopy walk at Lolegaon is pleasant through the day.

Higher up, rhododendrons flower in the forests around Lava, Rishyap and the edges of Neora Valley in spring, a few weeks later the higher you go. Days in town are warm enough for a shirt by noon, while mornings at Rishyap still need a fleece. Spring is also a good time for paragliding at Deolo, on the calm, clear mornings before clouds build.

The cost is the view. Dust and heat haze from the plains build up through April and May, and Kanchenjunga often shows only for an hour after dawn, if at all. Mid-May to mid-June also brings the Bengal school holidays, when rooms in Kalimpong and Lava fill and prices rise.

sections.heading: Monsoon, landslides and Neora's closure
paras: The monsoon usually arrives in mid-June and stays into September. Rain can fall for days without a break, cloud sits on the ridges, and landslides close roads at short notice. NH10, the main road from Siliguri via Sevoke and Teesta Bazar, has had repeated landslide and flood closures since the October 2023 Teesta flood, and monsoon months are when closures are most likely. Diversions via Lava or via Darjeeling and Peshok add hours.

There is another side to these months. The forests are at their greenest, waterfalls such as Changey Falls near Kolakham run full, and homestays that turn guests away in October will often discount a quiet July week. Travellers who come for rain, cloud and a book on the veranda can have a good, cheap stay, as long as they arrive with time to spare and no fixed train to catch.

Neora Valley National Park closes from mid-June to mid-September, and rafting at Teesta Bazar stops through the high-water months. If you do travel in the monsoon, keep a spare day in your plan, travel in the morning, and stay put when your host says the road is bad. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Festivals worth planning around
paras: Festival dates follow lunar calendars and shift each year, so confirm them locally before you book.
list: Losar, February or March: Tibetan New Year in the monasteries, including Zang Dhok Palri on Durpin, with prayers and family visits.
Dashain and Tihar, October to November: Dashain coincides with Durga Puja, and Tihar with Diwali. Lamps, marigolds and sel roti fill the town; so do holidaymakers from Kolkata.
Namsoong, December or January: the Lepcha New Year, kept by Lepcha communities around Kalimpong with food, songs and gatherings.
Gaeboo Achyok day, 20 December: Lepchas gather at the ruins of Damsang fort near Pedong for the birth anniversary of the Lepcha chief who built it.
Christmas: the churches of Kalimpong's old Scottish mission hold services, and the week to New Year is one of the busiest of the year for rooms.

sections.heading: Crowds, prices and when to book
paras: Three periods fill Kalimpong: the Durga Puja and Diwali holidays in October or November, Christmas to New Year, and mid-May to mid-June. In those weeks the state lodges at Deolo, Durpin, Lava and Lolegaon sell out early, homestays raise rates, and shared jeeps from Siliguri run full. Book four to six weeks ahead for Puja and New Year.

The quietest good weeks are mid-November to mid-December and late February to March. You get clear or fairly clear mornings, open roads in most years, and room to bargain politely on longer stays. Whatever month you choose, road and park status changes quickly here, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Kalimpong?
faqs.a: November is usually the best single month. The monsoon has cleared, Kanchenjunga is visible on most mornings, the Puja crowds have gone home and Neora Valley has reopened. October and the first half of December are almost as good, though October is busy with Dashain and Durga Puja holidaymakers. Book state lodges a few weeks ahead for any of these months.

Kalimpong town, at 1,247 m, very rarely sees snow. The higher villages do: Lava at about 2,195 m and Rishyap at 2,591 m get snow in some winters, usually in January or February. It is never guaranteed and may melt within a day or two. If snow is the point of your trip, keep your dates flexible and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Kalimpong worth visiting in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Only if you accept the trade-offs. From mid-June to September the hills are green and rooms are cheaper, but rain can last for days, mountain views are rare, Neora Valley is closed and landslides shut roads, including NH10, at short notice. Keep spare days, travel in the morning and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When can you see Kanchenjunga from Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Your best chance is October to mid-December, when Kanchenjunga is visible on most clear mornings until clouds build around 10 or 11 am. January and February also give clear dawns. From March the haze thickens, and from June to September the mountains are hidden on most days. Deolo, Durpin, Rishyap, Charkhole and Icchey Gaon give the best views.

faqs.q: When is Neora Valley National Park open?
faqs.a: Neora Valley National Park is usually open from mid-September to mid-June and closed through the monsoon, from mid-June to mid-September. Entry is by forest permit with a compulsory local guide, arranged at the Lava range office. The best months for walking are October to December and March to May. Dates and rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Kalimpong crowded during Durga Puja?
faqs.a: Yes. Durga Puja and Dashain in October, and Diwali and Tihar soon after, bring large numbers of holidaymakers from Kolkata and the plains. State lodges at Deolo, Durpin, Lava and Lolegaon sell out, homestays raise their rates and shared jeeps from Siliguri run full. Book four to six weeks ahead, or come in mid-November when the rush has passed.

faqs.q: What is the weather like in Kalimpong in December?
faqs.a: December in Kalimpong is cold, dry and usually clear, with town temperatures of roughly 7–17 °C and colder nights at Lava, Rishyap and Lolegaon. Mountain views are very good. It is also festival season: Gaeboo Achyok day on 20 December at Damsang near Pedong, the Lepcha New Year Namsoong, and Christmas, which fills rooms in the last week.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Kalimpong in winter?
faqs.a: Pack for nights near freezing in the higher villages: thermals, a down or fleece jacket, a warm hat, gloves and thick socks. Homestay rooms are not heated, though hosts provide quilts. Add sunscreen and sunglasses for bright days, sturdy shoes for the walks to sunrise points, and a torch, since power cuts happen in the villages.

faqs.q: Is May a good time to visit Kalimpong?
faqs.a: May is good for warm weather, flowers and birds, but not for mountain views. Haze and afternoon clouds hide Kanchenjunga on many days, and pre-monsoon showers begin late in the month. Mid-May to mid-June is also the Bengal school holiday season, so rooms in Kalimpong and Lava fill and prices rise. Book ahead if May is your only option.
